Joint drills on the 38th parallel cut short. The UAE embargoes Iran. Israel bombs a Syria that Washington is courting.

Five stories where the real subject wasn't where the border runs, but who stands behind it.

5 ways the map moved — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Ulchi Freedom Shield ends today — cut from 11 days to 5 at Washington's request, after Trump ordered the drills scaled back (Guardian, Al Jazeera, BBC, NYT).

Seoul's president wants wartime command back.

The 1953 line isn't a border. Seoul sits ~50 km from it.

2/ The UAE has imposed an indefinite trade embargo on Iran over missile strikes Tehran denies (Al Jazeera). Trump threatened to bomb Oman for negotiating over Hormuz (Guardian).

Oman's Musandam peninsula — the strait's southern jaw — is an exclave, cut off by the UAE.

3/ Israel struck a Syrian air base, drawing US irritation (NYT). Damascus opened Assad's nuclear file to UN inspectors; Lebanon stopped sheltering ex-regime officials (Al Jazeera).

For 14 years Syria's decisive lines were internal. Now every one that matters is external.

4/ Trump paused a 50% tariff on Canadian goods and said Keystone XL "may be awoken from the grave" (Guardian; also BBC, Al Jazeera, NYT).

The line ran Hardisty, Alberta to Steele City, Nebraska. Cancelled 2021.

Alberta's oil is landlocked. That's the whole negotiation.

5/ Belgium's largest wildfire in a century burned peat, pine and trails in the High Fens on the German border — half the size of Manhattan (Guardian, DW).

Peat bogs are waterlogged by definition.

When the wettest ground on the map burns, the fire map has moved north.

The historical parallel — the Syrian civil war in four frames.

2015: Islamic State black across the east. 2016: it shrinks. 2019: Turkish strips appear in the north. 2021: regime red covers nearly all of it.

The colour changed hands in 2024. The shape didn't.

Full issue — five stories, five maps, every source linked — in Lines & Legends.
